steps: Let X_1, X_2, X_3 each act on finite-particle vectors as z^dag(f_j^+) + z(f_j^-) + K_j, where K_j preserves particle number and K_j Omega = 0; consider the one-particle component P_1 X_1 X_2 X_3 Omega.
Each factor X_j changes particle number by +1 (via z^dag), by -1 (via z) or by 0 (via K_j), and a term of X_1 X_2 X_3 Omega lands in H_1 only if the three changes sum to +1.
Three steps from {+1, -1, 0} sum to +1 only in the patterns (+1,+1,-1) or (+1,0,0) in some order, because exactly one 0 would leave two steps of size 1 that must sum to +1, which is impossible.
Hence P_1 X_1 X_2 X_3 Omega contains no term with exactly one number-preserving factor K_j; its terms are the three z/z^dag terms and terms containing two of the K_j.
In a (+1,0,0) pattern the rightmost factor acts on Omega, where z(f_3^-) Omega = 0 and K_3 Omega = 0, so the rightmost factor is z^dag(f_3^+) and the only two-K term is K_1 K_2 z^dag(f_3^+) Omega.
For the Cadamuro-Tanimoto field phi~(f) = phi(f) + chi(f) this gives P_1 phi~(f_1) phi~(f_2) phi~(f_3) Omega = g + chi_1(f_1) chi_1(f_2) f_3^+, with g the L8 phi-phi-phi one-particle component.
Using (chi_1(f) xi)(theta) = c f^+(theta + i pi/3) xi(theta - i pi/3) twice, chi_1(f_1) chi_1(f_2) f_3^+ equals A(theta) = c^2 f_1^+(theta + i pi/3) f_2^+(theta) f_3^+(theta - 2i pi/3).

traps.text: So single-chi terms chi(f_j) appear in P_1 X_1 X_2 X_3 Omega at degree 3 and must be matched against the L8 defect D.
traps.why: One zero step plus two steps of size 1 cannot sum to +1; no one-chi term lands in H_1.

traps.text: The chi_2 part of the CT field, and with it the bootstrap equation S(theta + i pi/3) = S(theta) S(theta + 2i pi/3), also enters P_1 at degree 3.
traps.why: chi_n for n >= 2 acts inside H_n and only contributes to P_2, P_3 at degree 3; only chi_1 enters P_1.

steps: Let psi_1, psi_2, psi_3 be entire with the reflection identity conj psi(w) = psi(conj w + i pi), and set A(theta) = c^2 psi_1(theta + i pi/3) psi_2(theta) psi_3(theta - 2i pi/3) with c^2 real.
Shifting the argument by i pi gives A(t + i pi) = c^2 psi_1(t + 4i pi/3) psi_2(t + i pi) psi_3(t + i pi/3) for every real t.
Applying the reflection identity to each factor gives conj psi_1(t + 4i pi/3) = psi_1(t - i pi/3), conj psi_2(t + i pi) = psi_2(t) and conj psi_3(t + i pi/3) = psi_3(t + 2i pi/3) for real t.
Since c^2 is real, conj A(t + i pi) = c^2 psi_2(t) psi_1(t - i pi/3) psi_3(t + 2i pi/3) for every real t.
With B(t) = c^2 psi_3(t + i pi/3) psi_2(t) psi_1(t - 2i pi/3), subtraction gives conj A(t + i pi) - B(t) = c^2 psi_2(t) [psi_1(t - i pi/3) psi_3(t + 2i pi/3) - psi_1(t - 2i pi/3) psi_3(t + i pi/3)].
The L8 defect is D(t) = -2 pi r psi_2(t) [psi_1(t - 2i pi/3) psi_3(t + i pi/3) - psi_1(t - i pi/3) psi_3(t + 2i pi/3)], whose bracket is the negative of the bracket in conj A(t + i pi) - B(t).
With the CT normalization c^2 = 2 pi |R_2| = -2 pi r, valid because Im R_2 > 0 so r < 0, the two expressions give conj A(t + i pi) - B(t) = -D(t) for every real t.
Adding to D(t) = conj g^cont(t + i pi) - g~(t) gives conj[(g^cont + A)(t + i pi)] = (g~ + B)(t) identically: the CT chi-chi term cancels the L8 degree-3 residue defect exactly.

traps.text: Use the W_R-type shift psi(theta - i pi/3) xi(theta + i pi/3) for W_L coefficients; it produces the same cancellation of D.
traps.why: That multiplier is unbounded for W_L test functions and its arguments are shifted by i pi relative to D, so it does not cancel.

traps.text: The cancellation holds for either residue sign: take c^2 = 2 pi |R_2| also when Im R_2 < 0.
traps.why: If Im R_2 < 0 then 2 pi |R_2| = +2 pi r and the total defect doubles to 2D instead of vanishing.

traps.text: Therefore Omega is separating for the CT wedge algebra, reversing L8's non-separation result.
traps.why: The identity only removes the degree-3 obstruction on H_1; separation stays OPEN and hinges on the self-adjoint-extension problem.

steps: Let f be in C_c^infty(W_L) and suppose f^+ has an L^2-bounded analytic continuation to the strip R + i(-eps, 0), which is the condition for f^+ to lie in CT's domain of chi_1(g).
The Fourier transform f^+(w) is entire and 2 pi i-periodic, because the mass-shell vector p(theta) = m(cosh theta, sinh theta) satisfies p(theta + 2 pi i) = p(theta).
The phase bound |exp(i p(t+is).x)| <= exp(2m |x| e^{|t|}) gives |f^+(t + is)| <= ||f||_1 exp(C e^{|t|}) for all s, with C = 2m sup over supp f of |x|.
The sub-mean-value inequality on discs of radius eps/2 turns the L^2 bounds on horizontal lines in -eps < Im w < 0 into a uniform pointwise bound, so f^+ is bounded on the line Im w = -eps/2.

Since f^+ is bounded on 0 <= Im w <= pi for wedge support, Phragmen-Lindelof on the strip -eps/2 <= Im w <= 0 with growth exp(C e^{|t|}), order 1 < pi/(eps/2), makes f^+ bounded on -eps/2 <= Im w <= pi.
By 2 pi i-periodicity the line Im w = -eps/2 is also the upper edge of pi <= Im w <= 2 pi - eps/2, a strip of width below pi, so Phragmen-Lindelof again bounds f^+ there.
Thus f^+ is bounded on a full period strip, hence by 2 pi i-periodicity bounded on all of C, and Liouville's theorem makes f^+ constant.
Riemann-Lebesgue gives f^+(t) -> 0 as t -> +infinity, since |p(t)| -> infinity and f is in L^1, so the constant is zero and f^+ vanishes identically.
Hence for real f_2, f_3 in C_c^infty(W_L) with f_3^+ nonzero, phi~(f_3) Omega = f_3^+ is not in Dom chi_1(f_2) = Dom phi~(f_2), so phi~(f_2) phi~(f_3) Omega is undefined for CT's literal operators.

traps.text: Every wedge one-particle vector f^+ lies in CT's literal domain of chi_1, so the cubic vectors phi~(f_1) phi~(f_2) phi~(f_3) Omega are defined for CT's operators.
traps.why: Lemma 4.1: f^+ is in Dom chi_1 only if f^+ = 0; CT's literal domain excludes all nonzero wedge one-particle vectors.

traps.text: Phragmen-Lindelof then bounds f^+ on the entire strip -pi <= Im w <= pi directly, with no periodicity argument needed.
traps.why: Phragmen-Lindelof needs bounds on both edges of the strip; the lower strip is only controlled via the periodic upper edge Im = -eps/2.

steps: For real f in C_c^infty(W_L), chi_1(f) = c M_h T, where T xi = xi(. - i pi/3) on L^2-bounded continuations to -pi/3 < Im < 0 and M_h multiplies by the bounded function h = f^+(. + i pi/3).
By the Paley-Wiener theorem for strips, the shift T equals exp((pi/3) K) with K = -i d/dtheta, so T is a positive self-adjoint operator.
Since M_h is bounded and T is self-adjoint, the adjoint is chi_1(f)^* = (c M_h T)^* = c T M_{conj h}.
The reflection identity conj f^+(w) = f^+(conj w + i pi) gives conj h(theta) = f^+(theta + 2i pi/3) on R, so chi_1(f)^* xi = c T [f^+(. + 2i pi/3) xi].
For entire xi, applying the shift gives (chi_1(f)^* xi)(theta) = c f^+(theta + i pi/3) xi(theta - i pi/3), the same formula as chi_1(f) but on a larger domain.

On the finite-particle vectors, phi(f) is symmetric and Dom chi(f) lies inside them, so a finite-particle xi is in Dom phi~(f)^* iff xi is in Dom chi(f)^*, and then phi~(f)^* xi = phi(f) xi + chi(f)^* xi.

For any X_j with phi~(f_j) inside X_j inside phi~(f_j)^*, if Omega is in Dom(X_1 X_2 X_3), each X_j acts on the finite-particle intermediate vectors as phi(f_j) + chi(f_j)^*, so P_1 X_1 X_2 X_3 Omega = g + A.
If also Omega is in Dom(X_3 X_2 X_1) and g + A is in Dom S_1, uniqueness of the H^2 continuation identifies it with g^cont + A, so S_1(g + A) = conj(g^cont + A)(. + i pi) = g~ + B.
Hence the L8 degree-3 Tomita contradiction S_1 P_1 Psi_ord != P_1 Psi_rev can never be produced against the CT field, for any choice of extensions X_j.

traps.text: Since A is entire, A is in L^2 and Omega lies in Dom(X_1 X_2 X_3) for every extension X_j.
traps.why: For L8-ordered wedge test functions |A(+-5)| ~ 1e26 numerically, so A is (numerically) not in L^2 and Omega is outside the domain.

traps.text: So the degree-3 Tomita test is passed on wedge-polynomial vectors and certifies that Omega is separating for the CT wedge algebra.
traps.why: The hypotheses of Cor. 3.4 are generically never met on wedge-polynomial vectors; the test is vacuous and separation stays OPEN.

steps: In the [T] S-symmetry convention the cyclic permutation rho_k acts as D(rho_k) = M_{S_k} F_k, with S_k(theta) = prod_{j<k} S(theta_k - theta_j) and F_k moving slot k to the front, so F_k X_1 = X_k F_k where X_k = Delta_k^{1/12}.
S is analytic and bounded on the closed strip 0 <= Im u <= pi/6, has |S| = 1 on R and |S(u + i pi/6)| <= 1 by (S8), so Phragmen-Lindelof gives |S| <= 1 on that whole strip.

For chi' in Dom(X_k), the family y -> S_k(theta + i(pi/6 - y) e_k) chi'(theta - i y e_k), 0 <= y <= pi/6, is analytic in theta_k with L^2 norms bounded uniformly in y, because |S| <= 1 on 0 <= Im <= pi/6.
The boundary value at y = 0 is S_k^#(theta) chi'(theta) with S_k^#(theta) = prod_{j<k} S(theta_k - theta_j + i pi/6), and the boundary value at y = pi/6 is S_k(theta) (X_k chi')(theta).
By Paley-Wiener for the strip, S_k^# chi' lies in Dom(X_k) and X_k(S_k^# chi') = M_{S_k} X_k chi', since X_k is the shift theta_k -> theta_k - i pi/6.
Applying this to chi' = F_k chi gives D(rho_k) X_1 chi = M_{S_k} X_k F_k chi = X_k M_{S_k^#} F_k chi, so D(rho_k) X_1 is contained in X_k V_k with V_k := M_{S_k^#} F_k.
The operator norm satisfies ||V_k|| <= sup |S_k^#| <= 1, because each factor S(theta_k - theta_j + i pi/6) has modulus at most 1 by (S8).

traps.text: The same intertwining works in the opposite S-symmetry convention (as in PAP Lemma 3.2), with dressings S(theta_j - theta_k + i pi/6) bounded on the strip.
traps.why: In the opposite convention the strip of continuation ends on the pole of S at -i pi/6, so the dressing is not bounded; the convention matters.

steps: For psi in D_nat^(2) = H_2 intersect Dom(D_1), with D_1 = Delta_1^{1/6}, the operator T_2 = 2 P_2 D_1 acts as T_2 psi = D_1 psi + D(rho_2) D_1 psi, where D(rho_2) is unitary.
Expanding the square, ||T_2 psi||^2 = 2 ||D_1 psi||^2 + 2 Re <D_1 psi, D(rho_2) D_1 psi>, so coercivity reduces to nonnegativity of the real cross term.
In the fibre of total momentum p write psi = e^{ips} g_p(u) with u = theta_2 - theta_1; the cross term then depends only on g_p, which ranges over S-symmetric functions in H^2(0 < Im u < pi/3).
By S-symmetry and the edge-of-the-wedge theorem g_p continues analytically across R, and g_p(0) = S(0) g_p(0) = -g_p(0), so g_p(0) = 0.

Shifting the contour to Im u = pi/3, using g(-v) = S(-v) g(v) and the bootstrap equation, gives cross term = integral of S(v + 2 pi i/3) |g(v)|^2 dv, the simple pole at v = 0 killed by the double zero.
Condition (S7), Re S(v + 2 pi i/3) >= 0 on R with infimum 216 sqrt3 - 374 > 0 for S_{1/2}, makes the real part of that integral nonnegative for every g in the domain.
Hence ||T_2 psi||^2 >= 2 ||D_1 psi||^2 for all psi in D_nat^(2), a two-particle coercivity bound with no lower-order ||psi|| term.

traps.text: The pole of S(v + 2 pi i/3) at v = 0 is harmless simply because its residue is purely imaginary, so the contour identity holds on all of D_nat^(2).
traps.why: An imaginary residue only explains boundedness of Re S; validity on the whole domain needs g_p(0) = 0 from S(0) = -1 and analytic continuation.

steps: Let psi be in H_2 intersect Dom(X_1) and suppose the a.e. function r(psi) := e^{pi t_1/6} (X_1 psi)^ + e^{pi t_2/6} (V_2 X_1 psi)^ lies in L^2(R^2), where ^ is the Fourier transform.
The band projection Q'_N, the Fourier multiplier by 1(N-1 < t_1 + t_2 <= N), commutes with X_1, with V_2 and with P_2, so r(Q'_N psi) = 1_N r(psi).
On the band, t_1 <= N/2 or t_2 <= N/2; there e^{pi t_1/6}|(X_1 psi)^| is bounded by e^{pi N/12}|(X_1 psi)^| or by |r| + e^{pi N/12}|(V_2 X_1 psi)^|, so e^{pi t_1/3}(Q'_N psi)^ is in L^2.
Hence each band piece Q'_N psi lies in D_nat^(2) = H_2 intersect Dom(D_1), with D_1 = X_1^2 = Delta_1^{1/6}.
For chi in D_nat^(2), the intertwining D(rho_2) X_1 in X_2 V_2 gives (T_2 chi)^ = r(chi), so (T_2 Q'_N psi)^ = 1_N r(psi).
The coercivity ||T_2 chi||^2 >= 2 ||D_1 chi||^2 on D_nat^(2) applied to chi = Q'_N psi gives 2 ||D_1 Q'_N psi||^2 <= ||1_N r(psi)||^2 for every N.
Summing over the disjoint bands N gives ||e^{pi t_1/3} psi^||^2 <= (1/2)||r(psi)||^2 < infinity, so psi lies in D_nat^(2), (T_2 psi)^ = r(psi) and ||D_1 psi|| <= ||r(psi)||/sqrt2.

traps.text: Since r(psi) is in L^2 and T_2 is closed, psi is in D_nat^(2) immediately, with T_2 psi equal to the inverse Fourier transform of r(psi).
traps.why: r(psi) is only an a.e. formal expression; membership in Dom(D_1) must first be shown band by band before closedness or coercivity can be used.

steps: Fix a band N and Psi in Dom(F_3) intersect H_3 intersect ran Q_N, where F_3 = 3 A^* A with A = X_1 P_3; put R := (F_3 Psi)^ and Phi := X_1 Psi.
The a.e. identity of Lemma 1.3 gives e^{pi t_1/6} Phi^ + e^{pi t_2/6} (V_2 Phi)^ = R - e^{pi t_3/6} (V_3 Phi)^ almost everywhere in (t_1, t_2, t_3).
V_2 acts only in slots 1 and 2, and D(tau_12) commutes with partial Fourier transform in slot 3, so for a.e. t_3 the fibre psi_{t_3} := [Psi^(., ., t_3)]^v lies in H_2 and, by Fubini, in Dom(X_1).
For a.e. t_3 the identity reads r(psi_{t_3}) = R(., ., t_3) - e^{pi t_3/6} (V_3 Phi)^(., ., t_3), which is in L^2(R^2).
The two-particle lemma (Q_2^+) applied to psi_{t_3} gives the integral of e^{2 pi t_1/3} |Psi^(t_1, t_2, t_3)|^2 over (t_1, t_2) at most (1/2) ||r(psi_{t_3})||^2.
Integrating over t_3 <= M and using ||V_3|| <= 1 gives a(M)^2 := integral over t_3 <= M of e^{2 pi t_1/3} |Psi^|^2 <= (1/2)(||R|| + e^{pi M/6} ||Phi||)^2.
Because Xi^(t_1, t_2, t_3) = Psi^(t_1, t_3, t_2) for the slot-swapped vector Xi, the same bound holds for Xi on the region t_2 <= M: b(M) = a(M).

traps.text: Letting M tend to infinity in the bound on a(M) gives e^{pi t_1/3} Psi^ in L^2(R^3) directly, so Psi is in Dom(D_1).
traps.why: The bound grows like e^{pi M/6}; it only controls the region t_3 <= M, and the regions must be glued via the unitary C with L^1 kernel.

traps.text: Estimate the three terms separately as uncorrelated data and bound e^{pi t_1/6} Phi^ alone in the region t_1 ~ t_2 -> infinity, t_3 -> -infinity.
traps.why: Lane D Prop D7: uncorrelated three-term cancellation is possible there; the pair must be treated as an S-symmetric two-particle fibre.

steps: Put f := e^{pi t_1/3} Psi^ and g := e^{pi t_1/3} Xi^ with Xi the slot-2/3 swap of Psi; for a.e. t_1 the slices satisfy f_{t_1} = C g_{t_1}, C the Fourier image of multiplication by S(theta_3 - theta_2), unitary.
Since S - 1 is analytic on -pi/6 < Im u < pi/3 with exponential decay on closed substrips, a contour shift gives S - 1 = integral of k(s) e^{ius} ds with k in L^1(R).
Therefore C acts on slices as (C h)(t_2, t_3) = h(t_2, t_3) + integral of k(s) h(t_2 + s, t_3 - s) ds, translating t_2 and t_3 in opposite directions.
In the band N-1 < t_1 + t_2 + t_3 <= N, for t_1 > L the slice f_{t_1} is supported in t_2 + t_3 < 2M with M = (N - L)/2, hence inside {t_3 <= M} union {t_2 <= M}.
Splitting g_{t_1} at t_2 = M + R_0 and using Minkowski's inequality, ||1_{t_2 <= M} f_{t_1}|| <= ||1_{t_2 <= M + R_0} g_{t_1}|| + eps(R_0) ||g_{t_1}||, with eps(R_0) the L^1 mass of k on |s| > R_0.
Integrating over t_1 > L with the fibre bounds a(M), b(M + R_0), and bounding t_1 <= L by e^{2 pi L/3} ||Psi||^2, gives e^{pi t_1/3} Psi^ in L^2, so the band vector Q_N Psi lies in Dom(D_1).

traps.text: Because C is unitary, ||1_{t_2 <= M} f_{t_1}|| = ||1_{t_2 <= M} g_{t_1}||, so the t_2 <= M region is controlled by b(M) directly.
traps.why: The cutoff 1_{t_2 <= M} does not commute with C; only the L^1 tail estimate on k controls the leakage across the cutoff.

steps: A := X_1 P_3 is closed and densely defined on L^2(R^3), F_3 := 3 A^* A is self-adjoint and reduced by H_3, D_nat = H_3 intersect Dom(D_1) lies in Dom(F_3), and F_3 = T_3 = 3 P_3 D_1 on D_nat.
The band projections Q_N = 1(N-1 < t_1 + t_2 + t_3 <= N) are multipliers in the total momentum, so they commute with X_1, P_3 and every V_k, hence with A, A^* and F_3, and preserve H_3.
The fibre-and-glue argument gives Q_N Psi in Dom(D_1) for every Psi in Dom(F_3) intersect H_3 and every N, so the partial sums of Q_N Psi over |N| <= L lie in D_nat.
These partial sums converge to Psi, and F_3 applied to them equals the partial sums of Q_N F_3 Psi, which converge to F_3 Psi, so the restriction of F_3 to H_3 is the closure of T_3.
Pairwise (S7) positivity Re <D(rho_k) D_1 Psi, D(rho_l) D_1 Psi> >= 0 on D_nat ([T] Prop 4.13) gives the coercivity ||T_3 Psi||^2 >= 3 ||D_1 Psi||^2.
Coercivity together with closedness of D_1 makes T_3 closed on D_nat, so T_3 equals its closure F_3 restricted to H_3 and is self-adjoint on D_nat.
Stripping the unimodular multipliers, chi_3(xi) = (M^{(x)3})^* P_3 (Delta^{1/6} (x) 1 (x) 1) P_3 M^{(x)3}, so chi_3(xi) is self-adjoint on Tanimoto's domain and its deficiency index m_3 = 0.
Conjugating by J_3, using chi'_3(eta) = J_3 chi_3(J_1 eta) J_3, shows chi'_3(eta) is also self-adjoint on its Tanimoto domain (Theorem A at n = 3).

traps.text: Essential self-adjointness of T_3 on D_nat already means T_3 is self-adjoint on D_nat, so Theorem A is finished.
traps.why: Self-adjointness on D_nat itself also needs T_3 closed there, which uses the (S7) coercivity ||T_3 Psi||^2 >= 3 ||D_1 Psi||^2.

traps.text: The same induction then proves Theorem A_n for every n, so N3 establishes m_n = 0 for all n.
traps.why: The referee accepted only n = 3; the all-n sketch in N3 section 1.6 is INFERENCE-grade until written out and refereed separately.

steps: Let m >= 2, chi in D_nat^(m) = H_m intersect Dom(D_1) with D_1 = Delta_1^{1/6}, and u := D_1 chi; let G_1 be the permutations fixing slot 1 and rho_k the cyclic coset representatives with rho_k(1) = k.
Each D(g) with g in G_1 acts only in slots 2..m, so it commutes with D_1, and since chi is S-symmetric, D(g) u = D_1 D(g) chi = D_1 chi = u.
For k != l, <D(rho_k) u, D(rho_l) u> = <u, D(rho_k^{-1} rho_l) u>, and rho_k^{-1} rho_l lies in the coset tau_{1a} G_1 with a = rho_k^{-1}(l) != 1.
Because G_1 fixes u, the cross term equals <u, D(tau_{1a}) u>; for a >= 3, tau_{1a} = tau_{2a} tau_{12} tau_{2a} with D(tau_{2a}) unitary and fixing u, so every cross term equals <u, D(tau_{12}) u>.

Fibring over the Fourier variables t'' = (t_3, ..., t_m), almost every fibre of chi lies in D_nat^(2), so <u, D(tau_{12}) u> is an integral over t'' of two-particle cross terms, each >= 0 by (S7)-positivity.
By the coset formula T_m chi = sum_k D(rho_k) u, so ||T_m chi||^2 = m ||u||^2 + m(m-1) <u, D(tau_{12}) u> >= m ||D_1 chi||^2 for every chi in D_nat^(m).
If chi_i in D_nat converge to chi with T_m chi_i -> y, the coercivity makes D_1 chi_i Cauchy, and closedness of D_1 gives chi in D_nat with T_m chi = y, so T_m is closed on D_nat.

traps.text: Pairwise positivity only bounds ||T_m chi||^2 >= m ||D_1 chi||^2 - C ||chi||^2, so the coercive estimate carries an unavoidable lower-order term.
traps.why: All m(m-1) cross terms equal the nonnegative <u, D(tau_12) u>, so the bound holds exactly with constant m and no ||chi|| term.

steps: For S = S_{1/2}, S - 1 is analytic on the strip -pi/6 < Im u < pi/3 and satisfies |S(u) - 1| = O(e^{-|Re u|}) uniformly on closed pole-free substrips.
Hence S - 1 is in L^1 on every horizontal line in that strip, and the vertical sides of rectangle contours vanish in the limit by the exponential decay.
Cauchy's theorem then gives k(s) := (2 pi)^{-1} integral of (S(u) - 1) e^{-ius} du = (2 pi)^{-1} e^{sy} integral of (S(x + iy) - 1) e^{-isx} dx for every y in (-pi/6, pi/3).
Choosing y = -(pi/6 - delta) for s >= 0 and y = pi/3 - delta for s <= 0 gives |k(s)| <= C_delta e^{-(pi/6 - delta) s} for s >= 0 and |k(s)| <= C_delta e^{-(pi/3 - delta)|s|} for s <= 0.
So k is a continuous function in L^1(R), and since S - 1 and k are both L^1 and continuous, Fourier inversion gives S(u) - 1 = integral of k(s) e^{ius} ds for all real u.
Consequently the Fourier image of multiplication by S(theta_l - theta_j) is 1 + K_l with (K_l g)(t) = integral of k(s) g(t - s e_l + s e_j) ds, a unitary smearing with ||K_l|| <= ||k||_1.
The tail mass eps(R) := integral over |s| > R of |k(s)| tends to 0 as R -> infinity by dominated convergence, which controls leakage of this smearing across momentum cutoffs.

traps.text: By symmetry of the argument, k(s) decays like e^{-(pi/3)|s|} in both directions s -> +infinity and s -> -infinity.
traps.why: The pole of S at -i pi/6 limits the downward contour shift, so for s >= 0 the decay rate is only pi/6 - delta.

steps: Let psi be in H_m intersect Dom(X_1) with Q_N psi = psi for one band B_N = {N-1 < t_1 + ... + t_m <= N}, let r := r_m(psi) be in L^2, and put f := e^{pi t_1/3} psi^.
Because psi^ vanishes outside the band B_N, for a.e. t_1 the slice f_{t_1} vanishes outside the set where t_2 + ... + t_m <= N - t_1.
For t_1 > 0 on that set, t_2 + ... + t_m < N, so min over l >= 2 of t_l is below M := N/(m-1), giving ||f_{t_1}|| <= sum over j = 2..m of ||1_{t_j <= M} f_{t_1}||.

The S-symmetry Psi = M_{Sigma_j} U_j Psi, whose Fourier image C_j is a unitary L^1 smearing, gives ||1_{t_j <= M} f_{t_1}|| <= ||1_{t_m <= M + R_0} f_{t_1}|| + eps_j(R_0) ||f_{t_1}|| for 2 <= j <= m-1.
Choosing R_0 with eps' := sum_j eps_j(R_0) <= 1/2 gives ||f_{t_1}|| <= (m-1) ||1_{t_m <= M + R_0} f_{t_1}|| + eps' ||f_{t_1}|| for a.e. t_1 > 0.
Since the slices have finite norm a.e., the eps' term can be absorbed, giving ||f_{t_1}|| <= 2(m-1) ||1_{t_m <= M + R_0} f_{t_1}|| for a.e. t_1 > 0.
Squaring, integrating over t_1 > 0 and using the fibre bound over slot m gives the integral of |f|^2 over t_1 > 0 at most 4(m-1)(||r|| + e^{pi(M + R_0)/6} ||X_1 psi||)^2, which is finite.
Together with the integral of |f|^2 over t_1 <= 0 being at most ||psi||^2, this shows e^{pi t_1/3} psi^ is in L^2, so the band vector psi lies in Dom(D_1).

traps.text: This band estimate gives ||D_1 psi|| <= C ||r|| with C independent of N, so summing it over bands finishes the induction.
traps.why: The bound grows like e^{pi M/6} with M = N/(m-1); it is only qualitative, and the bands are summed using (S7) coercivity instead.

steps: Assume (Q_{m-1}^+): every psi in H_{m-1} intersect Dom(X_1) with r_{m-1}(psi) in L^2 lies in D_nat^(m-1) with ||D_1 psi|| <= ||r_{m-1}(psi)||/sqrt(m-1) and no ||psi|| term.
Take psi in H_m intersect Dom(X_1) with r := r_m(psi) in L^2(R^m) and set psi_N := Q_N psi, the projection onto the momentum band B_N.
Q_N commutes with X_1 and with every V_k, so psi_N lies in H_m intersect Dom(X_1) and r_m(psi_N) = 1_{B_N} r, which is in L^2.
The band claim, proved from (Q_{m-1}^+) by the fibre bound over slot m and the L^1 gluing, gives psi_N in D_nat^(m) for every band N.
On D_nat^(m) the Fourier transform of T_m chi equals r_m(chi), so (T_m psi_N)^ = 1_{B_N} r for every N.
The coercivity ||T_m chi||^2 >= m ||D_1 chi||^2 on D_nat^(m) then gives m ||D_1 psi_N||^2 <= ||1_{B_N} r||^2 for every band N.
The bands partition R^m, so monotone convergence gives m times the integral of e^{2 pi t_1/3} |psi^|^2 = m sum_N ||D_1 psi_N||^2 <= ||r||^2 < infinity.
Hence psi lies in D_nat^(m) with ||D_1 psi|| <= ||r_m(psi)||/sqrt(m) and (T_m psi)^ = r_m(psi), which is (Q_m^+), closing the induction.

traps.text: It suffices to carry an induction hypothesis with a lower-order term, ||D_1 psi|| <= C(||r_{m-1}(psi)|| + ||psi||), as in [T] Prop 4.7.
traps.why: The record stresses that without the no-||psi||-term form the fibre bound over slot m is not uniform in the spectator momentum t_m.

steps: Let A := X_1 P_n on K_n = L^2(R^n) with Dom(A) = {Psi : P_n Psi in Dom(X_1)}; since P_n is bounded, (P_n X_1)^* = X_1 P_n = A.
Density of D_nat in H_n (Lane F Prop F3) makes A densely defined, so P_n X_1 is closable, A is closed, and A^* = closure(P_n X_1).
By von Neumann's theorem F_n := n A^* A is self-adjoint and nonnegative on K_n.
Because A(1 - P_n) = 0 and ran A^* lies in H_n, the subspace H_n reduces F_n, and the part of F_n in H_n, with domain Dom(F_n) intersect H_n, is self-adjoint in H_n.
For Psi in D_nat, A Psi = X_1 Psi lies in Dom(X_1), inside Dom(A^*), and F_n Psi = n P_n D_1 Psi = T_n Psi, so D_nat lies in Dom(F_n) with F_n = T_n there.
Conversely, for Psi in Dom(F_n) intersect H_n, Psi lies in Dom(X_1) and the a.e. identity r_n(Psi) = (F_n Psi)^ holds, so r_n(Psi) is in L^2.
The a-priori estimate (Q_n^+) then puts Psi in D_nat, so Dom(F_n) intersect H_n = D_nat and T_n equals the self-adjoint part of F_n in H_n.
Hence T_n = n P_n Delta_1^{1/6} P_n is self-adjoint and nonnegative on D_nat, and its deficiency indices are (0, 0): m_n = 0 for every n (Theorem A_n).

traps.text: A = X_1 P_n is densely defined automatically, because X_1 is densely defined on K_n.
traps.why: Density of Dom(A) needs H_n intersect Dom(X_1) dense in H_n; this is exactly where the cited density (H4) of D_nat enters.

traps.text: Since T_n is contained in the self-adjoint operator F_n restricted to H_n and both are nonnegative, T_n is already self-adjoint.
traps.why: A restriction of a self-adjoint operator need not be self-adjoint; the reverse inclusion Dom(F_n) intersect H_n in D_nat from (Q_n^+) is essential.

traps.text: T_n is symmetric and nonnegative, so its deficiency indices are equal, and therefore m_n = 0.
traps.why: Equal deficiency indices only guarantee self-adjoint extensions exist; m_n = 0 needs the domain identification Dom(F_n) intersect H_n = D_nat.

steps: By [T] section 2.4, chi_1(xi) = U_xi^* Delta^{1/6} U_xi with Dom = U_xi^* H^2(S_{-pi/3,0}), where U_xi multiplies by xi_0(theta + 2 pi i/3), a unimodular boundary value.

U_xi^{(x)n} multiplies by the permutation-symmetric function prod_k xi_0(theta_k + 2 pi i/3), so it commutes with coordinate permutations and with every M_{S(theta_{k+1} - theta_k)}, hence with D(sigma) and P_n.
The factors of U_xi^{(x)n} in slots 2..n commute with Delta^{1/6} (x) 1 (x) ... (x) 1, so chi_1(xi) (x) 1 (x) ... (x) 1 = (U_xi^{(x)n})^* D_1 U_xi^{(x)n} with domain (U_xi^{(x)n})^* Dom(D_1).
Therefore Dom chi_n(xi) = (U_xi^{(x)n})^* D_nat and, in the [T] section 2.4 normalisation, chi_n(xi) = (U_xi^{(x)n})^* (n^{-1} T_n) U_xi^{(x)n}.
Unitary equivalence preserves self-adjointness, so Theorem A_n makes chi_n(xi) self-adjoint on Tanimoto's domain for every n.
The antiunitary (J_n Psi)(theta) = conj Psi(theta_n, ..., theta_1) satisfies J_n D(tau_{k,k+1}) J_n = D(tau_{n-k,n-k+1}), using conj S(u) = S(-u) on R, so J_n commutes with P_n.
Since chi'_n(eta) = J_n chi_n(J_1 eta) J_n with J_1 eta in [T]'s class and antiunitary conjugation preserves self-adjointness, chi'_n(eta) is self-adjoint on its Tanimoto domain.
Taking orthogonal direct sums over n, chi(xi) and chi'(eta) are each self-adjoint on the Fock space on their natural direct-sum domains.

traps.text: The formula chi_n(xi) = U^*(n^{-1} T_n) U and the bound ||chi_n Psi|| >= n^{-1/2} ||(chi_1 (x) 1...)Psi|| hold whichever of [T]'s normalisations of chi_n is used.
traps.why: [T] section 2.3 uses n P_n(...)P_n; there chi_n = U^* T_n U and the constant becomes n^{1/2}.

traps.text: Hence the CT operators generate a wedge-local Haag-Kastler net.
traps.why: Self-adjointness of each operator separately gives nothing about strong commutativity, wedge-locality or the net.

steps: In the Fring-Mussardo-Simonetti conventions the Bullough-Dodd potential is 2 e^{g phi} + e^{-2g phi} with B(g) = 2g^2/(4 pi + g^2); setting B = 1/2 gives 4g^2 = 4 pi + g^2.
Solving 4g^2 = 4 pi + g^2 gives g^2 = 4 pi/3, so the exponent -2g of the term e^{-2g phi} has alpha^2 = (2g)^2 = 16 pi/3.
With the canonical field phi and X = sqrt(2 pi) phi of covariance -log, the vertex e^{alpha phi} equals e^{gamma X} with gamma^2 = alpha^2/(2 pi), so the -2g term has gamma^2 = 8/3.
Gaussian multiplicative chaos in d = 2 is nondegenerate iff gamma^2 < 4 and in L^2 iff gamma^2 < 2, so e^{-2g phi} with gamma^2 = 8/3 is Euclidean L^1 but not L^2.
The chaos moments E M(B)^p are finite iff p < 2d/gamma^2 = 4/(8/3), so the free-field chaos of e^{-2g phi} has moments only of order p < 3/2.
For the sharp-time field in d = 1 the chaos is nondegenerate iff gamma^2 < 2; since gamma^2 = 8/3 >= 2, the Wick-normalised time-zero density of e^{-2g phi} vanishes.

traps.text: Since e^{-2g phi} is in the Euclidean L^1 regime, its sharp-time version is a nonzero Q-space multiplication operator, so H = H_0 + V works.
traps.why: Time-zero chaos needs gamma^2 < 2 in d = 1; at gamma^2 = 8/3 the Wick-normalised time-zero density converges to 0.

traps.text: At g^2 = 4 pi/3 both exponents are below the Euclidean L^2 threshold alpha^2 < 4 pi, so the AHK74 construction applies.
traps.why: (2g)^2 = 16 pi/3 > 4 pi; both exponents are L^2 only for B < 2/5, and AHK74 needs support in (-sqrt(4 pi), sqrt(4 pi)).

steps: The Glimm-Jaffe / Hoegh-Krohn local-perturbation route builds local algebras from e^{itH_l} with H_l = H_0 + V_l, where V_l must be a nonzero positive Q-space function of the time-zero field.
The time-zero free field phi_0 of any mass m_0 > 0 has covariance kernel (1/2 pi) K_0(m_0|x|) = -(1/2 pi) log|x| + O(1), so it is log-correlated in dimension d = 1 with gamma^2 = alpha^2/(2 pi).

For alpha^2 >= 4 pi one has gamma^2 >= 2 = 2d, the critical or supercritical chaos regime, so V_eps = integral of h(x) :e^{alpha phi_0(x)}:_eps dx tends to 0 in probability while E V_eps = integral of h.
At B = 1/2 the exponent alpha = -2g has alpha^2 = 16 pi/3 > 4 pi, so the Wick-normalised time-zero interaction of the e^{-2g phi} term is the zero function.

Hence for every B >= 2/5 the Bullough-Dodd Hamiltonian is not H_0 plus a multiplication operator in the Lagrangian's normal ordering and must come from the Euclidean measure via the OS transfer matrix.
Therefore the Glimm-Jaffe / Hoegh-Krohn local-perturbation net is unavailable at B = 1/2, and the Schlingemann Euclidean-to-Minkowski theorem is the replacement bridge.

traps.text: Take V_l as the cutoff Wick exponential of the time-zero field, integrated against h, and use finite propagation speed to get local algebras at B = 1/2.
traps.why: Proposition 3.2: at alpha^2 = 16 pi/3 >= 4 pi the Wick-normalised time-zero integral vanishes in probability, so V_l = 0.

steps: Let mu be an E(2)-invariant, reflection-positive probability measure on S'(R^2) that is locally absolutely continuous (LAC) with respect to a free field mu_0 of mass m_0 > 0, with Euclidean net A(U) = L^infty(Sigma_U^germ, mu).
For real nonzero h in C_c^infty(R) and an approximate time-delta delta_eps, phi(h (x) delta_eps) converges to phi(h (x) delta_0) in L^2(mu_0), because h (x) delta_0 lies in H^{-1}(R^2).

By LAC the same convergence holds in mu-probability, so the sharp-time field phi(h (x) delta_0) is mu-measurable for the germ sigma-algebra of a bounded piece of the time-zero line and is invariant under time reflection.
Hence F := arctan phi(h (x) delta_0) is a bounded, real, reflection-invariant element of A(e) intersect A(-e), i.e. an element of the fixed-point algebra B(e) for the half-space e.
Under mu_0, phi(h (x) delta_0) is a centred Gaussian with variance (1/2)<h, (-d_x^2 + m_0^2)^{-1/2} h> > 0, and arctan is injective, so every level set {F = c} is mu_0-null.
By LAC each level set {F = c} is also mu-null, so F is not mu-a.s. constant and B(e) is not C1, which is Schlingemann's time-zero condition (TZ).

Schlingemann's Theorem 3.7 then yields a Poincare-covariant Haag-Kastler net of C*-algebras, and weak closure keeps locality because commutants are weakly closed, giving a net of von Neumann algebras.

traps.text: Hence Bullough-Dodd at B = 1/2 has a Haag-Kastler net via Theorem S, since the Euclidean Lagrangian measure is available.
traps.why: No published OS theorem gives the infinite-volume E(2)-invariant BD measure at B = 1/2; tightness, rotation invariance, LAC and clustering are OPEN.

traps.text: LAC of the infinite-volume BD limit follows by the routine P(phi)_2 DLR argument, since the interaction is a positive local density.
traps.why: The e^{-2g phi} conditional density is not quasilocal and lies in the L^1-not-L^2 chaos window; the referee downgraded LAC (E5) to OPEN.

traps.text: The resulting net therefore has two-particle S-matrix S_{1/2}, identifying it with the program's target net.
traps.why: Identifying the S-matrix of any constructed BD theory with S_{1/2} is OPEN; no Lagrangian model has a proved rapidity-dependent S-matrix.

steps: Let nu_n converge weakly to mu on S'(R^2), with nu_n restricted to Sigma_Lambda equal to rho_n mu_0 and sup_n of the integral of Psi(rho_n) d mu_0 = C_Lambda finite, for a convex superlinear Psi bounded below.
By the de la Vallee-Poussin criterion the densities rho_n are uniformly integrable in L^1(mu_0 restricted to Sigma_Lambda).
By the Dunford-Pettis theorem a subsequence of rho_n converges weakly in L^1 to some rho >= 0 with integral of rho d mu_0 equal to 1.

For F = G(phi(f_1), ..., phi(f_k)) with G bounded continuous and supp f_i in Lambda, the integrals of F d nu_n = F rho_n d mu_0 converge both to the integral of F rho d mu_0 and to the integral of F d mu.
These cylinder functions form a multiplicative class generating Sigma_Lambda, so the monotone class theorem gives mu = rho mu_0 on Sigma_Lambda: mu is absolutely continuous there.
Since F -> integral of Psi(F) d mu_0 is convex and strongly lower semicontinuous, it is weakly lower semicontinuous, so the limit density satisfies integral of Psi(rho) d mu_0 <= C_Lambda.

traps.text: Each nu_n is absolutely continuous on Sigma_Lambda, so weak convergence alone already makes mu absolutely continuous on Sigma_Lambda.
traps.why: Absolute continuity is not preserved by weak limits; the uniform entropy-type bound is what gives uniform integrability.

traps.text: For Bullough-Dodd at B = 1/2 the uniform local entropy bound sup_L H(nu_L | mu_0) on Sigma_Lambda is routine, so LAC of the limit is settled.
traps.why: Controlling the non-quasilocal e^{-2g phi} boundary factor in the L^1-not-L^2 window is OPEN; Lemma 3.3 only reduces LAC to this bound.

steps: Consider V = lambda_1 :e^{g phi}: + lambda_2 :e^{-2g phi}: with a massless kinetic term, whose free measure is invariant under constant shifts phi -> phi + c.
The shift phi -> phi + c maps the couplings (lambda_1, lambda_2) to (lambda_1 e^{gc}, lambda_2 e^{-2gc}), so the only shift-invariant combination of the couplings is lambda_1^2 lambda_2.
Since E e^{alpha phi_eps} = eps^{-alpha^2/(4 pi)}, the Wick exponential :e^{alpha phi}: has scaling dimension alpha^2/(4 pi) and its coupling has mass dimension 2 + alpha^2/(4 pi).
Hence lambda_1^2 lambda_2 has mass dimension 2(2 + g^2/(4 pi)) + (2 + g^2/pi) = 6(1 + g^2/(4 pi)), which equals 8 at g^2 = 4 pi/3.
So the massless model is a one-parameter family with mass scale m proportional to (lambda_1^2 lambda_2)^{1/8}, and the 2:1 coefficient ratio in the Lagrangian is a convention.
A massive free field breaks the shift symmetry and adds the independent relevant term (m_0^2/2) phi^2, so the Hoegh-Krohn model with atoms at g and -2g is Bullough-Dodd plus a mass term.

traps.text: So a construction of the massive exponential model with atoms at g and -2g (e.g. Frohlich-Park, if valid) gives the integrable Bullough-Dodd net at B = 1/2.
traps.why: The massive model is a two-parameter deformation, BD plus a mass term, not expected integrable; the integrable model is the massless case.

steps: The gauge function h(u) = (1/8) sinh(u/2) prod_c (sinh u + ic), c in {sqrt3/2, -1/2, -1}, satisfies h(u)/h(-u) = S(u); put H(theta) = prod_{i<j} h(theta_j - theta_i) and W = |H|^2.
For an adjacent transposition sigma the identity S^sigma(theta) H(theta^sigma) = H(theta) is exactly h(x)/h(-x) = S(x); both sides are cocycles for the symmetric group, so it holds for every sigma.
Consequently D(sigma)(H G) = H (G o sigma) for every measurable G, so H G lies in the S-symmetric space H_n if and only if G is a symmetric function.

Since ||H Phi||^2 = integral of W |Phi|^2 and H vanishes only on coincidence hyperplanes, every Psi in H_n equals H Phi with Phi = Psi/H symmetric, so Phi -> H Phi is unitary from L^2_sym(R^n, W) onto H_n.
For Psi in D_nat write X_1 Psi = H G; then T Psi = n P_n (H G) = H (n/n!) sum over sigma of G o sigma, by the covariance D(sigma)(H G) = H (G o sigma).

For sigma with sigma(1) = k, G(theta^sigma) = [H(theta^sigma - i pi/3 e_1)/H(theta^sigma)] Phi(theta - i pi/3 e_k), and the bracket equals c_k(theta) = prod_{j != k} h(theta_j - theta_k + i pi/3)/h(theta_j - theta_k).
Each k occurs (n-1)! times, so in the gauge (T Psi)(theta) = H(theta) sum_k c_k(theta) Phi(theta - i pi/3 e_k) with c_k = prod_{j != k} B(theta_k - theta_j) and B(u) = h(-u + i pi/3)/h(-u).

traps.text: For Psi in D_nat the gauged function Phi = Psi/H is holomorphic on the whole slot-1 strip -pi/3 < Im theta_1 < 0.
traps.why: H vanishes at depth pi/6 on coincidences (zero of h at i pi/6), and Phi can have simple poles there for vectors in D_nat.

steps: Every pair-type gauge for S has the form h' = h E with E even meromorphic, and its pair coefficient is B'(u) = B(u) E(u - i pi/3)/E(u), where B(u) = h(-u + i pi/3)/h(-u).
Evenness of E gives R(u) := E(u - i pi/3)/E(u) with R(u + i pi/3) R(-u) = 1, so Gamma_B(u) := B(u + i pi/3) B(-u) is invariant under change of pair gauge.
Substituting B(u) = h(-u + i pi/3)/h(-u) and h(x)/h(-x) = S(x) gives Gamma_B(u) = S(u + i pi/3)/S(u).
The bootstrap identity S(x) = S(x + i pi/3) S(x - i pi/3) turns this into Gamma_B(u) = 1/S(u - i pi/3), which has a simple pole at u = i pi/2 from the simple zero of S at i pi/6.

For the Ruijsenaars coefficient V_g(u) = s(u - ig)/s(u) with s(z) = sinh(z/2), Gamma_{V_g}(u) = s(u + i pi/3 - ig) s(u + ig)/(s(u + i pi/3) s(u)), with poles only in 2 pi i Z union (-i pi/3 + 2 pi i Z).
Gamma of any product c prod_j V_{g_j} has poles only in that set, since numerator zeros can only cancel poles, whereas Gamma_B has a pole at i pi/2 outside it.
By gauge invariance of Gamma, B is not pair-gauge equivalent to any c prod_j V_{g_j}: the Bullough-Dodd compression is not a hyperbolic Ruijsenaars operator with period 2 pi, in any pair gauge.

traps.text: Since the BD compression factors as the Lee-Yang Ruijsenaars operator times a bounded pair dressing, it is a hyperbolic Ruijsenaars operator for a suitable coupling, so the HR/BDKK eigenfunction transform diagonalises it.
traps.why: The gauge invariant Gamma_B = 1/S(u - i pi/3) rules out any RCM form; numerically the compressions of e_1, e_2 do not even commute.

traps.text: This pole argument alone already excludes Ruijsenaars coefficients sh(pi(u - ig)/omega_2)/sh(pi u/omega_2) for every period omega_2.
traps.why: For other omega_2 (e.g. pi/6) the pole set of Gamma_V can contain i pi/2; a separate periodicity argument is needed.

steps: For a period parameter omega_2 != 0, the Ruijsenaars coefficient V_g^{omega_2}(u) = sh(pi(u - ig)/omega_2)/sh(pi u/omega_2) is i omega_2-periodic, since numerator and denominator both change sign under u -> u + i omega_2.
Hence for one common omega_2 the gauge invariant Gamma of c prod_j V_{g_j}^{omega_2}, namely c^2 prod_j V_{g_j}^{omega_2}(u + i pi/3) V_{g_j}^{omega_2}(-u), is i omega_2-periodic.
If B were pair-gauge equivalent to such a product, gauge invariance would make Gamma_B(u) = 1/S(u - i pi/3) i omega_2-periodic, so i omega_2 would be a period of S.
A period p of S must map the pole multiset of S mod 2 pi i, simple poles i pi/3, 2i pi/3, -i pi/6, -5i pi/6 and a double pole -i pi/2, onto itself; all lie on iR, so Re p = 0.
The double pole at -i pi/2 is the only pole of its order, so p lies in 2 pi i Z, and therefore omega_2 lies in 2 pi Z without 0.
For such omega_2 the poles of Gamma_V lie in (-i pi/3 + 2 pi i Z) union 2 pi i Z, which misses the pole of Gamma_B = 1/S(u - i pi/3) at u = i pi/2, a contradiction.
Therefore the Bullough-Dodd compression is not a hyperbolic Ruijsenaars operator for any coupling and any period parameter, in any pair gauge.

traps.text: S is i pi-periodic, so omega_2 = pi is also allowed and must be checked separately.
traps.why: S(u + i pi) = 1/S(u), not S(u); the double pole at -i pi/2 forces every period of S into 2 pi i Z.

steps: For the free-fermion reference S_0 = -1, H_n = Lambda^n and T_0 = sum_k X_k is self-adjoint on D_0 = Lambda^n intersect Dom X_1, being multiplication by sum_k e^{pi t_k/3} in Fourier space.
For Psi in D_0 and x_k := X_k Psi, <x_k, x_l> = integral of e^{pi(t_k + t_l)/3} |Psi^|^2 >= 0, so sum_k ||x_k||^2 <= ||T_0 Psi||^2.

An admissible gauge h^ with h^(u)/h^(-u) = -S(u), h^ and 1/h^ holomorphic and bounded on 0 <= Im u <= pi/3, gives Q = prod h^(theta_j - theta_i) with D^S(sigma) M_Q = M_Q D^0(sigma), so M_Q maps Lambda^n boundedly invertibly onto H_n^S.
The slot-1 continuation of Q Psi_0 involves only h^(theta_j - theta_1 + iy), 0 <= y <= pi/3, bounded holomorphic, so M_Q D_0 = D_nat^S and K := M_Q^{-1} T_S M_Q = sum_k g_k X_k with bounded g_k.

With eps_k = g_k - 1, a pointwise bound |sum eps_k x_k|^2 <= beta_0 sum |x_k|^2 + alpha(theta) |sum x_k|^2, integrated using the positivity of <x_k, x_l>, gives ||(K - T_0) Psi|| <= a ||T_0 Psi|| for every a > a_n.
If a_n < 1 then ||(K - T_0)(T_0 + lambda)^{-1}|| < 1 for lambda > 0, so K + lambda = (1 + (K - T_0)(T_0 + lambda)^{-1})(T_0 + lambda) maps D_0 onto Lambda^n.
Then T_S + lambda = M_Q (K + lambda) M_Q^{-1} maps D_nat^S onto H_n^S, and a nonnegative symmetric operator with Ran(T_S + lambda) = H_n^S is self-adjoint, so m_n(S) = 0.

traps.text: A gauge with its zero at i pi/6 inside the strip works equally well, so any gauge with h^(u)/h^(-u) = -S(u) can be used.
traps.why: If Q vanishes in the open slot-1 strip, M_Q(Lambda^n intersect Dom X_1) != D_nat^S, so the exact similarity fails; the gauge must be lower.

traps.text: The numerical value a_3(S_{0.95})^2 = 0.969 < 1 therefore gives a proved, new proof that m_3 = 0 for Bullough-Dodd.
traps.why: (N) is NUMERICAL-ONLY, not interval-certified; the route is CONDITIONAL and superseded by the proved N3 Theorem A.

traps.text: With the same admissible gauge family the comparison theorem also reaches n = 4.
traps.why: At n = 4 the coincidence configurations force a_4^2 >= 0.899 + 0.294 > 1 for this gauge family.

steps: Let X be D_0 = Lambda^n intersect Dom X_1 with the graph norm of T_0, a Banach space independent of B, and A_B := K_B + 1 : X -> Lambda^n with K_B = M_{Q_B}^{-1} T_{S_B} M_{Q_B}.
Since K_B = sum_k g_k^B X_k and sum_k ||X_k Psi||^2 <= ||T_0 Psi||^2, one gets ||A_B - A_{B'}|| <= n^{1/2} sup over theta and k of |g_k^B - g_k^{B'}|.
The pair dressing rho^_B is uniformly bounded and sup-norm continuous in B on compact subsets of (0,1), so B -> A_B is norm continuous from X to Lambda^n.
K_B is closed on D_0, being similar to T_{S_B}, which is closed by T16 Prop 4.13 under (S7), and A_B is bounded below in L^2 because T_{S_B} >= 0.
A closed operator bounded below has closed range, and the open mapping theorem upgrades this to ||A_B Psi|| >= c_B ||Psi||_X in the graph norm.
Lower bounds persist under small norm perturbations, so on a compact interval I in (0,1) there is a uniform constant c > 0 with ||A_B Psi|| >= c ||Psi||_X for all B in I.
If A_{B_1} is onto, then A_B = A_{B_1}(1 + A_{B_1}^{-1}(A_B - A_{B_1})) is onto whenever ||A_B - A_{B_1}|| < c, and uniform continuity propagates onto-ness across I in finitely many steps.
Since onto-ness of A_B is self-adjointness of T_{S_B}, self-adjointness of the stripped compression holds for all B in (0,1) or for none.

steps: The Lee-Yang factor of the Bullough-Dodd S-matrix is f_{2/3}(t) = (sinh t + i sqrt3/2)/(sinh t - i sqrt3/2).
The addition formula gives sinh(t + 2 pi i/3) = -(1/2) sinh t + i (sqrt3/2) cosh t for real t.
Hence f_{2/3}(t + 2 pi i/3) = [-(1/2) sinh t + i (sqrt3/2)(cosh t + 1)] / [-(1/2) sinh t + i (sqrt3/2)(cosh t - 1)].
Multiplying by the conjugate denominator and using (cosh t + 1)(cosh t - 1) = sinh^2 t gives Re f_{2/3}(t + 2 pi i/3) = sinh^2 t / ((1/4) sinh^2 t + (3/4)(cosh t - 1)^2).
Since sinh^2 t = (cosh t - 1)(cosh t + 1) >= (cosh t - 1)^2, this ratio lies in [1, 4], so (S7) holds for f_{2/3} with a strict margin.
However Res_{2 pi i/3} f_{2/3} = i sqrt3 / cosh(2 pi i/3) = -2 sqrt3 i is not in iR_+, violating (S5), and |f_{2/3}(i pi/6)| = 2 + sqrt3 > 1 violates (S8).
So only the essential-self-adjointness half of T16 Prop 4.7 transfers to f_{2/3}, giving m_2(f_{2/3}) = 0, while closedness of the Lee-Yang compression for all n remains CONDITIONAL.

steps: The collar family satisfies J_2(d; g) = J_1 (J_1 + sqrt2 (2 - sqrt3)/(2 cosh d + 1)) with J_1 = g + 1/g + h_0, and J_1 vanishes at g_0 = e^{5 i pi/12}.
Differentiating in g at g_0, where J_1 = 0, gives D_2(d) = D_1 sqrt2 (2 - sqrt3)/(2 cosh d + 1) with D_1 = dJ_1/dg at g_0.
With the normalisation N lambda D_1 = 1/sqrt2, the elementary-field form factor is F^phi_2(z_1, z_2) = N lambda^2 D_2 f(d) = lambda (2 - sqrt3) f(d)/(2 cosh d + 1), with d = z_1 - z_2.
The residue at d = 2 i pi/3 is lambda (2 - sqrt3) f(2 i pi/3)/(2 sinh(2 i pi/3)) = lambda (2 - sqrt3) f(2 i pi/3)/(i sqrt3).
The identity f(z + i pi/3) f(z - i pi/3) r(z) = f(z) at z = i pi, with f(4 i pi/3) = f(2 i pi/3), f(i pi) = 1/mu and r(i pi) = (2 + sqrt3)/3, gives f(2 i pi/3)^2 = 3(2 - sqrt3)/mu.
With F^phi_1 = 1/sqrt2 and Gamma = -i Res F^phi_2 / F^phi_1, Gamma^2 = (2/3) lambda^2 (2 - sqrt3)^2 f(2 i pi/3)^2, and lambda^2 = sqrt3 mu gives Gamma^2 = 2 sqrt3 (2 - sqrt3)^3.
Since (2 - sqrt3)^3 = 26 - 15 sqrt3, Gamma^2 = 52 sqrt3 - 90 = -i Res_{2 i pi/3} S, and lambda < 0 with f(2 i pi/3) > 0 makes the bound-state coupling Gamma positive.

steps: The elementary-field two-particle form factor is F^phi_2(z_1, z_2) = lambda (2 - sqrt3) f(d)/(2 cosh d + 1) with d = z_1 - z_2 and lambda = -sqrt(sqrt3 mu) < 0.
The (1,1) kernel evaluates F^phi_2 at the crossed point d = x + i pi, where 2 cosh d + 1 = 1 - 2 cosh x <= -1 for real x.
The minimal form factor on the line Im = pi is real, f(x + i pi) = F_min(x + i pi)/mu, with 1 <= F_min(x + i pi) <= mu^2, so f(x + i pi) lies in [1/mu, mu].
Combining the signs lambda < 0 and 1 - 2 cosh x < 0, the kernel is phi_2(x) = |lambda| (2 - sqrt3) f(x + i pi)/(2 cosh x - 1), a strictly positive real-analytic function.
Evenness of phi_2 follows from f(i pi + x) = f(i pi - x), and the bounds on f give phi_2(x) between |lambda|(2 - sqrt3)/(mu(2 cosh x - 1)) and |lambda|(2 - sqrt3) mu/(2 cosh x - 1).
Hence phi_2 never vanishes and decays like e^{-|x|}, unlike the exponential members e^{a phi}, whose (1,1) kernels tend to the nonzero constant F0 lambda^2 J_c^2.

traps.text: Because phi_2 decays like e^{-|x|}, the LSZ decay of the elementary field removes the n^2 growth of the matched-pair pieces seen for e^{a phi}.
traps.why: The growth uses a fixed residual pair at bounded separation where phi_2 > 0; only the single number B_0 changes, not the n^2 combinatorics.

steps: Let h in C_c^infty(R^2) be real and nonzero, and O a nonempty open set of pairs (theta, eta) with theta != eta; the (1,1) kernel is B^phi(theta; eta) = H_h(P(theta) - P(eta)) phi_2(theta - eta).
Since phi_2 > 0 everywhere, B^phi(theta; eta) = 0 exactly when the Fourier-Laplace transform H_h vanishes at P(theta) - P(eta), with P(theta) = (cosh theta, sinh theta).
H_h is the Fourier-Laplace transform of a nonzero compactly supported function, so it is entire on C^2 and not identically zero.
The map (theta, eta) -> P(theta) - P(eta) has Jacobian determinant -sinh(theta - eta), which is nonzero on O.
By the inverse function theorem the image of O under this map contains a nonempty open set V in R^2.
If H_h vanished on V it would vanish identically by the identity theorem for real-analytic functions, so B^phi(theta_0; eta_0) != 0 for some (theta_0, eta_0) in O.

traps.text: So the no-go construction needs a genericity assumption on h, holding only for h with H_h(P(-2) - P(1)) != 0.
traps.why: Any nonzero real h works: the triple can be moved inside a small ball O around (-2, 1), and some point of O has B^phi != 0.

steps: Take unit product vectors Phi_n, Psi_n in H_n with residual rapidities near (theta_0, eta_0), B^phi_0 != 0, and n - 1 spectator packets near y_0 with nu_0 = (S(y_0 - theta_0) S(eta_0 - y_0) - 1)/2 != 0.
W_(r,k) maps H_n into H_{n-k+r}, so only diagonal degrees (r, r) with r <= 3 contribute to <Phi_n, phi^{<=6}(h) Psi_n>, and W_(0,0) drops because Phi_n and Psi_n are orthogonal.

The kinematic residue axiom splits W_(3,3)[K^{phi,+}] into the two-pair density insertion X^phi_2, a one-pair term with the regular (2,2) kernel, and a principal-value (3,3) term; the fully matched parts vanish.
The two-pair piece satisfies |<Phi_n, X^phi_2 Psi_n>| >= C(n-1, 2) |nu_0|^2 |B^phi_0| m_ug/2, since each chosen spectator pair contributes the phase nu_0 and the residual kernel B^phi_0.

The principal-value parts are bounded by finite sup-norms on compact separated windows and made smaller than n^2 |nu_0|^2 |B^phi_0| m_ug/16 by narrowing the spectator windows to width eps delta^2 n^{-5/2}.
Hence |<Phi_n, phi^{<=6}(h) Psi_n>| >= n^2 |nu_0|^2 |B^phi_0| m_ug/8 for large n, with m_ug independent of n.
The energy spreads of Phi_n, Psi_n are below 1 around N_n ~ n cosh y_0, so some shell block Z_{M'} phi^{<=6}(h) Z_{N'} with M' - N' in [1,4] has norm >= c N_n^2, violating CUT (7).
Since ||(H+1)^alpha Psi_n|| <= C n^alpha, no bound |<chi, phi^{<=6}(h) psi>| <= C ||chi|| ||(H+1)^alpha psi|| holds for alpha < 2, so the linear energy bound fails for the degree-6 truncation.

steps: Split {1..q} = A u B with q >= 2 and shift the B-rapidities by a real L; the label sum J_q(z_A, z_B + L; g) contains cross factors K(a_v, a_w; z_v - z_w - L) for v in A, w in B.
Each cross factor is a product of r(zeta - L), and r(zeta) - 1 = (1 - sqrt3)/(2 cosh zeta - 1) = O(e^{-|Re zeta|}), so J_q = J_|A|(z_A; g) J_|B|(z_B; g) + O(e^{-|L|}) uniformly for g in compacts.
The error term is a Laurent polynomial in g of bounded degree, so by Cauchy's formula on a fixed circle around g_0 its g-derivative at g_0 is also O(e^{-|L|}).
Differentiating the leading term at g_0 gives D_|A| J_|B|(g_0) + J_|A|(g_0) D_|B|, which vanishes because J_p(g_0) = 0 for every p >= 1.
The cross factors of the minimal form factor f tend to 1 and stay bounded, so the elementary-field form factor obeys F^phi_q(z_A, z_B + L) = O_{q,z}(e^{-|L|}) as L -> +-infinity.
By contrast the exponential members satisfy F^{(g)}_q(z_A, z_B + L) -> F^{(g)}_|A|(z_A) F^{(g)}_|B|(z_B), which is nonzero in general.

steps: Let J be an antiunitary operator with J Omega = Omega and M a von Neumann algebra for which Omega is cyclic and separating; then Omega is cyclic and separating for J M J as well.
For A in M, the Tomita operator of J M J satisfies S_{JMJ}(J A J Omega) = J A^* Omega = J S_M J (J A J Omega), so S_{JMJ} = J S_M J.
Writing S_M = J_M Delta_M^{1/2} gives S_{JMJ} = (J J_M J)(J Delta_M^{1/2} J), and uniqueness of the polar decomposition yields Delta_{JMJ} = J Delta_M J and J_{JMJ} = J J_M J.
Because J is antiunitary, (J Delta_M J)^{it} = J Delta_M^{-it} J, so the modular group of J M J is Delta_{JMJ}^{it} = J Delta_M^{-it} J.
The Fock conjugation J commutes with the boosts U(0, s), so Delta_{M_T}^{it} = U(0, -2 pi t) for the right-wedge algebra M_T is equivalent to Delta_{M_L}^{it} = U(0, 2 pi t) for M_L := J M_T J.
Likewise J^2 = 1 gives J_{M_T} = J if and only if J_{M_L} = J, so the Bisognano-Wichmann data transport between M_T and M_L with no wedge-duality input.
If in addition the modular conjugation equals the Fock conjugation, J_{M_T} = J, then Tomita-Takesaki gives M_T' = J_{M_T} M_T J_{M_T} = J M_T J = M_L, i.e. wedge duality.

steps: By L8 Theorem 2, for the ZF wedge algebra M_0 = {e^{i phi(f)} : f real in C_c^infty(W_L)}'' on the Fock space of S_{1/2}, the vacuum Omega is not separating.
Omega is separating for a von Neumann algebra M exactly when A Omega = 0 with A in M forces A = 0.
If a von Neumann algebra M contains M_0 and Omega is separating for M, then every A in M_0 with A Omega = 0 lies in M and hence vanishes, so Omega would be separating for M_0.
This contradicts L8 Theorem 2, so no von Neumann algebra containing M_0 has Omega as a separating vector.
Hence a repaired left-wedge algebra cannot be M_0 enlarged by bound-state operators; the ZF exponentials themselves must be replaced, as in CT's e^{i phi~(f)} with phi~ = phi + chi.

steps: The known deformation procedures (Longo-Witten endomorphisms, warped convolution, Bischoff-Tanimoto) multiply a Borchers triple's scattering function by a function bounded and analytic on 0 < Im theta < pi.
Products of functions bounded and analytic on the strip 0 < Im theta < pi are again bounded and analytic there, so deforming a pole-free seed never creates poles in the physical strip.
S_{1/2} = f_{2/3} f_{-1/6} f_{-1/2} has poles at i pi/3 and 2i pi/3 in the physical strip, so it is not obtainable by deformation from any pole-free Borchers triple.
Any deformation seed must therefore be S_{1/2}/g with g bounded analytic on the strip, and so it carries the poles at i pi/3 and 2i pi/3 itself.
The natural seed f_{2/3} (with g = f_{-1/6} f_{-1/2}) has Res_{2i pi/3} f_{2/3} = 2i sin(2 pi/3)/cosh(2i pi/3) = -2 sqrt3 i, opposite in sign to R_2 = i(52 sqrt3 - 90), so it violates (S5).
Hence deformation moves the problem to a seed with the same poles, i.e. back to the Cadamuro-Tanimoto bound-state route, and is a dead end as an independent route.
